sections.text: Introduction

This method covers the 
determination of the turbidity of drinking water, industrial water and 
industrial waste water. The nephelometric method for determining the turbidity 
covers the measurements of relative turbidity and is also applicable to the 
measurements of low turbidity

The first draft was initiated by 
chemist: Hoda Ahmed Abd-Allah; reviewed by director chemist: Hoda Hassanen; 
revised by quality control chemist: Mohamed Mosbah Mokpel, and accepted by eng. Fathy 
Mahmoud Ragab, approved by eng. Awad M. Fatthy; Head Sector of Talkha Power Station.

This document is accepted by eng. Samir 
Abd El Gilil EDEPC MPIS coordinator, and certified by accountant; Mahmoud 
Mohamed Soliman; EDEPC admin and financial inspection, quality control General 
Director and supervisor of inspection and quality control head sector.
Significance

Nephelometric turbidity based on a 
measurement of the light-scattering characteristics of the particulate matter in 
the sample.
Summary

Nephelometric turbidity instruments measured scattered light at 90-deg. or 90 
and 270-deg.
angles to incident beam.

These instruments cannot be calibrated accurately in 
terms of
absolute turbidity, except in the case fluids having uniform-size particles that 
are less than approximately one fifth of the wavelength of incident light. 
Nephelos standards have been prepared by thoroughly mixing suitable amounts of 
finely divided titanium dioxide ( TiO2 ) into partially polymerized 
polystyrene. Alternatively, a suspension of formazine has been used as a 
turbidity standard formed by reacting hydrazine sulfate and hexamethylene 
tetramine under carefully controlled conditions.
Definitions

Turbidity: 
Reduction 
of transparency of a sample due to presence of a particulate matter.
Safety Precautions

The reagent 
 used must be of sufficiently high purity to permit its use without 
 lessening the accuracy of determination.

The sample must be taken as the applicable ASTM methods D 
 3370-76.

Make sure that the sample bottle is correctly 
labeled.

Make sure that the sample bottle is free from dust 
and dirt.

sections.text:
Tools and 
Equipment
Apparatus
Nephelometer or calibrated slit Turbidimeter.
Work to be Carried out
Calibration

Using 
nephelometric turbidity standards obtain readings with at least three separate 
standards with in order to calibrate the instrument.
Procedure

Instruments 
using Nephelometric Standards

Adjust 
firstly the instrument system physically and electrically in accordance 
with the manufactures instructions, then replace the standards by the sample 
in an optically identical tube and record the reading.

The 
straight line relationship for Tyndall effect for small amounts of scattered 
90-deg or 90 and 270-deg light produces proportional readings for nephelometric 
turbidity standards up to approximately 100 nephelos units. Therefore, the 
nephelometric turbidity of the sample can be calculated as the turbidity of the 
calibrated standard times the ratio of the readings.

sections.text: Instruments Using Transmitted Light From Calibrated Slit as Reference

Follow the 
manufacturer's instructions in detail. This type of turbidimeter utilizes a fixed ratio of scattered light to transmitted light 
intensity.

Adjusts the quantity of light for transmission 
from the single light source until the observer matches the final intensity of 
the light for the different paths, by using a calibrated slit. The instrument uses a special cell for the 
sample.

Estimate the mid-point of the interval of 
uniform-light intensity for the two fields by rotating the dial in one direction 
only towards higher values, for all calibrated slit instruments. This eliminates errors caused by lost motion in the 
mechanism.

sections.text: Calculation
Calculate the nephelometric turbidity in nephelos units, as follows:
Nephelometric turbidity = AB
Where:
A = instrument reading of scattered light,
B = nephelos units per unit of instrument reading.
Report
Report results as nephelos units.
